strategies.name: Multi-Platform Detection Strategy for T1678 - Delay Execution

analytics.name: Analytic 1048
analytics.guidance: Correlated use of sleep/delay mechanisms (e.g., kernel32!Sleep, NTDLL APIs) in short-lived processes, combined with parent processes invoking suspicious scripts (e.g., wscript, powershell) with minimal user interaction.

tuning.description: Delay duration that distinguishes benign scripts from evasive behavior.
Legitimate parent-child combinations may differ across environments.
Different APIs may be used to invoke sleep (e.g., Sleep, NtDelayExecution).

analytics.name: Analytic 1049
analytics.guidance: Shell scripts or binaries invoking repeated 'sleep', 'ping', or low-level syscalls (e.g., nanosleep) in short-lived execution chains with no user or system interaction. Frequently seen in malicious cron jobs or payload stagers.

tuning.description: Environment-specific delay scripts may vary (sleep 300, ping -n 60, etc.).
Threshold for determining if delay is artificially extended.
Root vs. service user context alters risk profile.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: execve or nanosleep with no stdout/stderr I/O

analytics.name: Analytic 1050
analytics.guidance: Execution of AppleScript, bash, or launchd jobs that invoke delay functions (e.g., sleep, delay in AppleScript) with limited parent interaction and staged follow-on commands.

tuning.description: AppleScript vs shell scripts differ per threat and org.
Execution under user vs daemon context changes severity.
Amount of delay that distinguishes benign usage vs evasion.

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: launchd or osascript spawns process with delay command

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: delay/sleep library usage in user context
